_conditions: All times in ns unless stated otherwise. Values transcribed from the cited manufacturer datasheets (downloaded Oct 2026). 'delays' and 'checks' use the names the simulator's models read; some entries also carry extra, clearly named delays or checks (fmax, pulse widths, recovery) that no model reads yet. Per delay: 'max' = the larger of tPLH/tPHL (enable: tPZH/tPZL; disable: tPHZ/tPLZ) at the worst-case corner below; 'typ' = the larger typical; 'min' = the smaller guaranteed minimum over the same range as max. Where one name covers several datasheet arcs (several inputs or outputs), max and typ are the largest and min the smallest of them; 'detail' rows are [min, typ, max at 25 C, max over the corner range] per datasheet arc and transition, as printed (null = not given). Corners by family. 74F: max and min over the commercial range 0..70 C, VCC 4.5-5.5 V, CL 50 pF, RL 500 Ohm; typ at 25 C, 5 V, 50 pF. 74ABT: max and min over -40..85 C, VCC 4.5-5.5 V, CL 50 pF, RL 500 Ohm; typ at 25 C, 5 V. 74HCT: max over -40..85 C at VCC 4.5 V, CL 50 pF; as in timing_logic.json, 'typ' is the 25 C, 5 V, CL 15 pF typical (TI CD74HCT sheets) and 'typ_4V5_50pF' the 25 C, 4.5 V, 50 pF typical (TI SN74HCT sheets); build_timing.py prefers typ_4V5_50pF for HCT. HCT sheets give no min. 74ACT: max and min over -40..85 C, VCC 5 V +-0.5 V, CL 50 pF; typ at 25 C. Where a logic datasheet gives no typical, typ is estimated as build_timing.py does (0.6 x max for ACT) and listed under 'estimated' as '<name> typ'. Devices and memories (TL16C550C, 82C54, CF card, SRAM) have only guaranteed limits: their delays carry 'typ' equal to 'max' (the convention build_timing.py uses for the existing memories, so not listed as an estimate; a fraction-of-max typical would be optimistic for an access time) and 'min' where given. 'checks' are datasheet minimum requirements (setup, hold, pulse width, cycle) over the same range as max; names ending in 'MHz' are frequencies. 'estimated' lists every number that is not printed in the datasheet; 'notes' gives the reason. 'alt' lists a second source or second family with its own numbers: for worst-case use the datasheet of the vendor you buy, or the worse of the two. Where TI has two versions of an HCT part (SN74HCT and CD74HCT) the primary entry is the one with the worse maxima on most arcs. Availability is from each manufacturer's package addendum or product page (checked Oct 2026). Pin names are TI style (CLK, /CLR, /LOAD, ENP, ENT, RCO, /OE, /G); notes give the datasheet's own names where they differ.

ATF22V10CQZ-20.notes: 'Zero power': its input transition detection powers it down while its inputs are still, 5 uA typical, 100-120 maximum; clocked at 15 MHz, ICC 40 mA typical, 80 maximum (industrial). tPD: an input or a feedback to a non-registered output (tEA, tER 20 too); CLK->Q is tCO; tCF (clock to feedback) 8, so fMAX with internal feedback 45.5 MHz: not on the 50.35 MHz master clock. 74HCT05.notes: Test load: RL = 1 kOhm to VCC, CL = 50 pF (15 pF for the 'typ' column). 'A->Y' is tPZL (output pulled low, input rising); 'release' is tPLZ (output let go, input falling). Max at 25 C: 22 (tPZL), 20 (tPLZ). tPLZ only times the output transistor turning off (in Nexperia's 74HC05 waveform: output 10% of VCC above VOL); the rise to a logic high is then set by the pull-up and the net capacitance (about 0.7 RC to cross 1.5 V-2 V from 0 V), which the simulator must add. TTL input levels (VIH 2.0 V, VIL 0.8 V). Output may only be pulled up to VCC + 0.5 V.

CDC341.availability: TI CDC341DW (SOIC-20) and DWR active (package addendum, Oct 2026). Not obsolete.

CDC341.typ_cond: typ: estimated (25 C, 5 V limits are 3.5..4.5 ns)
CDC341.notes: tsk(o) (output to output, same part) 0.6 ns over 0..70 C (0.5 at 25 C); tsk(pr) (process skew, part to part under identical conditions) 1 ns; tsk(p) (|tPLH - tPHL|) 0.9 ns. typ is the midpoint of the 25 C min/max (no typical printed; A->Y 3.5..4.5, G->Y 2..3.8). G->Y is the 1G/2G gate input to the outputs. Supply must be 4.75-5.25 V, tighter than the logic. The recommended input clock is at most 80 MHz with one output bank loaded and 40 MHz with both banks loaded, so a 50 MHz (20 ns) clock driving all 8 outputs is outside the datasheet's operating conditions. Datasheet drift figures: about -0.05 ns per 10 C and +0.02..0.03 ns per 100 mV.

TL7705A.function: supply voltage supervisor (power-on reset), 4.55 V threshold
TL7705A.availability: TI TL7705ACD/ACDR (SOIC-8), ACPSR, AID/AIDR active; the DIP TL7705ACP and TL7705AIP are NRND. TI also makes a newer TL7705B (SLVS037O; not compared here).
TL7705A.max_cond: TL7705AC: 0..70 C; TL7705AI: -40..85 C; VCC up to 18 V
TL7705A.units: td in ms per uF of CT
TL7705A.reset_output: Two outputs. /RESET (pin 5, active low): open collector, sinks 16 mA at 0.4 V, needs a pull-up. RESET (pin 6, active high): open emitter, sources 16 mA at VCC - 1.5 V, needs a pull-down. Both rated to 18 V; both active while VCC is below threshold and for td after it recovers or after /RESIN is released.
TL7705A.notes: td = 1.3e4 x CT (s, F), i.e. 13 ms per uF, from the 'externally adjustable pulse duration' text. The switching table gives the output pulse duration only at CT = 0.1 uF: 0.65 min, 1.2 typ, 2.6 max ms; 'td min'/'td max' scale that linearly to per-uF figures (an assumption). Other timing: /RESIN pulse >= 0.4 us, /RESIN to RESET <= 1 us; output rise/fall 0.2 us driven, 3.5 us through a 4.7 kOhm pull-up/down. SENSE threshold 4.5-4.6 V at 25 C (15 mV hysteresis). Outputs are defined from VCC = 3 V (typ 2.5 V); function guaranteed from 3.6 V.

TL16C550C.availability: TI TL16C550CFNR (PLCC-44, socketable), PTR (LQFP-48), PFBR (TQFP-48) active; industrial TL16C550CIFNR, CIPTR. No DIP.
TL16C550C.max_cond: 0..70 C, VCC 4.75-5.25 V (5 V operation), data outputs CL 75 pF
TL16C550C.notes: For a non-multiplexed bus with ADS tied low. With ADS latching the address and chip selects, 'tAS ADS' is their setup to ADS rising (tsu1, 8 ns) and 'tAH ADS' their hold after it: the hold isn't in the notes taken from the datasheet, so 8 ns, the setup's figure, is an estimate. tAS = tAR/tAW (td8/td5, address valid before RD/WR active) 7 ns; with ADS used instead, address setup to ADS rising (tsu1) is 8 ns. tCS = tCSR/tCSW (td7/td4) 7 ns (8 ns to ADS). tAH = tRA (th7, address hold after RD) 20 ns; after WR (tWA, th4) only 10 ns, given as 'tAH WR'. tCH = tRCS/tWCS (th6/th3) 10 ns. tRD (tw7) and tWR (tw6) 40 ns. tDS (tsu3) 15 ns before WR inactive, tDH (th5) 5 ns. tRC = cycle time tcR = tcW = 87 ns (strobe 40 + address setup 7 + recovery 40); 'recovery' = td9/td6, RD or WR inactive to the next cycle, 40 ns. RD->D = td10 (tRVD) 45 ns, RD->D dis = td11 (tHZ) 20 ns, both at CL 75 pF. 'xin max MHz': oscillator/clock 16 MHz at 5 V (14.9 MHz at 3.3 V); XIN high and low 25 ns each. Strobes: /RD1 and /WR1 active low, RD2 and WR2 active high (use one, tie the other inactive). The 5 V supply range is 4.75-5.25 V.
TL16C550C.typ_cond: typ = max: the datasheet gives guaranteed limits only

82C54.notes: 82C54-10 column. The -12 grade (CS82C54-12Z) has identical bus timings; only TCLK min 80 ns (12.5 MHz) and TPWL 30 ns differ. The plain 8 MHz 82C54 is slower on the bus (tAR 30, tRR 150, TRD 120, TDF 85, TDW 140, TWD 25, TRV 200). RD->D = TRD (data delay from /RD); data is also not valid before TAD = 185 ns after the address ('A->D'). RD->D dis = TDF (5..65). tDW (95) equals the minimum /WR width, so write data must be valid by the time /WR falls. tRV (165) is the command recovery between any two strobes (read or write). WR->OUT = TWO (OUT delay from mode write); CLK->OUT = TOD; GATE->OUT = TODG. CLK and GATE timing (TGS, TGH, TPWH, TPWL) is referenced to the rising CLK edge. Not all parameters are tested (note 1). TTL-compatible inputs (VIH 2.0 V); outputs 2.5 mA.

CF.function: CompactFlash card in True IDE mode, PIO mode 0
CF.manufacturer: CompactFlash Association (spec), as repeated by card makers
CF.part_number: CF+ & CompactFlash spec rev 4.1, True IDE PIO mode 0
CF.datasheet: Delkin Devices C400 Series SLC Industrial CompactFlash Engineering Specification L5ENG00049 Rev. F (2018), section 4.14 'True IDE PIO Mode Read/Write Timing' (card states compliance with CF spec rev 4.1); cross-checked against Innodisk iCF4000 Rev 3.0 (Feb 2014), section 5.9.2.7 Table 12 (https://static.chipdip.ru/lib/012/DOC004012395.pdf): identical mode 0 numbers.
CF.availability: Industrial CF cards (e.g. Delkin, Innodisk, Transcend, Apacer) still sold; every CF card must support PIO mode 0 in True IDE mode. The CFA sells the spec itself; no free official copy found.
CF.max_cond: spec limits (all cards); the spec states loading only for -IOCS16 (1 LSTTL + 50 pF)
CF.notes: Mode 0 column. RD->D = t2 (8-bit register access, 290) - t5 (read data setup to -IORD rising, 50) = 240 ns: the latest a compliant card can put data out after -IORD falls if the host uses the minimum strobe width (derived, as requested). RD->D dis: t6 = 5 ns data hold (min), t6z = 30 ns tri-state (max) after -IORD rises. t2 is 290 ns for 8-bit register access and 165 ns for 16-bit data transfers ('t2 16-bit'). t2i: the spec gives no recovery time for modes 0-2 ('-'); 0 is entered so the check is vacuous, and the binding limit is t0 = 600 ns from one strobe assertion to the next (so after a 290 ns register strobe the strobe must stay negated >= 310 ns). t9 = address (and CS) hold after -IORD/-IOWR negation. t7/t8 = address valid to -IOCS16 assert/release (max), tA = IORDY setup, tB = IORDY pulse width (max); a card may extend a cycle with IORDY.
CF.typ_cond: typ = max: the datasheet gives guaranteed limits only
